text:
One thing first: the Dealectric page in my search results contained text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and discount code for the Bluetti AC180. You didn't ask for that and it isn't one of my picks, so I've left it out.

**Best for most campers (weekend, car or tent camping): a 250-500Wh unit**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W) is PowerStationGearLab's top pick for light weight and simplicity. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. [Buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W) has double the inverter output and can expand to 572Wh. It's the better pick if you want to run more demanding gear. [Buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "DC" variant. The same page lists it, but OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored it lower (50/100), so I'd rank it below the two above. [Buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) · [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W) is the budget pick. [Buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

**If you need more power (electric cooler, multi-day trips, van or overland)**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It's 39 lb, 2,200W, and listed under $900 on Amazon. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh) is TechRadar's camping pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is the best value in OutdoorGearLab's testing, at under $530 on sale. It has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's camping pick at about $1,079. It's IP65-rated and has a 5-year warranty. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**Quick sizing:** a phone charge takes about 10Wh, and a CPAP with the humidifier off takes about 30-60Wh per night. A 288Wh unit covers a weekend of devices, lights and a CPAP. Add a folding solar panel for longer trips.

The search results gave me no direct product-page URLs, only "Check price" buttons, so the links above go to the review pages that have the retailer buttons. Prices change often, so confirm the current price at checkout.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop), how many nights, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
